cards.f: Which average is not affected by extreme values?
cards.b: The median (the mean and the range are affected).
Plot running totals at the upper class boundary; start at the lowest boundary with 0.

cards.f: Reading quartiles from a cumulative frequency graph
cards.b: Median at n/2, LQ at n/4, UQ at 3n/4, p-th percentile at p% of n.
UQ − LQ: the spread of the middle 50% of the data.
Frequency ÷ class width (vertical axis of a histogram).
Represents frequency; frequency = frequency density × class width.
Positive: both increase together. Negative: one increases as the other decreases. Zero: no relationship.
Straight, by eye, following the trend, roughly equal points either side; need not pass through the origin.

gaps.s: The midpoint of the class 20 < t ≤ 30 is ___ .
A class of width 5 has frequency 15, so its frequency density is ___ .
A histogram bar has frequency density 2.4 and width 10, so its frequency is ___ .
Cumulative frequency is plotted at the ___ class boundary.
For 80 values, the upper quartile is read at the ___ th value.
Estimating values outside the range of the data is called ___ .

short.q: Estimate the mean: 0 < x ≤ 10 frequency 5; 10 < x ≤ 20 frequency 10; 20 < x ≤ 40 frequency 5.
A histogram has a class 20 < x ≤ 40 with frequency 30. Find the frequency density.
A cumulative frequency graph has 120 values. State the cumulative frequencies at which you read the median and the quartiles. If LQ = 22 and UQ = 41, find the IQR.
short.model: Median at 60, LQ at 30, UQ at 90. IQR = 41 − 22 = 19.

short.q: A scatter diagram shows revision hours against test score with positive correlation. Interpret this, and explain why predicting the score for 20 hours may be unreliable.
short.model: Students who revise for longer tend to score higher. 20 hours is outside the range of the data (extrapolation), so the trend may not continue.

short.q: Pets owned by 20 students: 0 pets 4, 1 pet 6, 2 pets 5, 3 pets 5. Find the mean and the median.
short.model: Σfx = 0 + 6 + 10 + 15 = 31, mean = 31 ÷ 20 = 1.55. The 10th and 11th values are 1 and 2, so the median is 1.5.
